_schema.what: The G-ADDR (dial ADDRESSABILITY) floor registry. One committed row per dial grid + per probe, holding the SHIPPED product dial's measured end-of-range behaviour on that instrument. A candidate bake clears the REGRESSION tier only when it reaches at least as far at BOTH ends as the row for the instrument it was measured on.
_schema.why: USER RULE 2026-09-04: 'floor and ceiling dial addressability is crucial ... any model that limits dial range cannot ship'. A dial that compresses at the ends cannot serve a target near the ends, which is where near-lossless product decisions live. SROCC is rank-invariant and structurally cannot see this; G1 (p5<=25, p95>=85) is far too loose to.
_schema.keyed_by: dial_grid_sha256 for the grid rows; probe_sha256 for the negative-tail and identity rows. An UNREGISTERED grid or probe is NOT-MEASURABLE / NOT-MEASURED, never a pass -- a bar you can dodge by choosing a friendlier instrument is not a bar.
_schema.owner: zensim-validate/src/dial_addressability.rs (embedded with include_str!, so a stale or missing file cannot silently disarm the gate). Consumed by bake_verdict's DIAL panel; emitted into --full-json at dial.addressability.
_schema.two_tiers: REGRESSION rows (A*) bar against the shipped dial's own value on the same instrument -- 'no worse at either end than what users have today'. CONTRACT rows (C*) are absolute product requirements. The shipped dial FAILS four contract rows today (C3/C4 negative tail, C5 identity band, C6 nothing-above-identity); those are standing defects recorded here, NOT bars invented for this gate, and the `incumbent` column in every report says so.
_schema.append_only: Rows are appended, never edited. A floor is a measurement of a specific bake on a specific instrument; changing it retroactively invalidates every verdict that quoted it. To raise a bar (a better dial ships), append a new row and retire the old one by label.

reference_bake.name: b_sdr_linear_cid80_inclwinsor_dense_dial_2026-07-07
reference_bake.role: ZensimProfile::B -- the SHIPPED SDR product dial as of 2026-09-04. Its end-of-range behaviour IS the regression floor: a replacement dial may not be worse at either end than the dial users have today.
reference_bake.measured_by: bake_verdict --bake <B> --dial-grid <grid> --negtail-probe <probe> --identity-probe <probe>, at zensim main 2026-09-04 (this lane's HEAD).
reference_bake.note: The gate keys on the GRID/PROBE sha, not on the bake, so a row stays readable if a re-pack changes the reference bake's bytes without changing its dial. The sha is recorded for provenance.

fixed_bars.provenance: mono/tied are the registered G3 bars (docs/EVAL_PANEL_REQUIREMENT.md), unchanged. The identity band is the shipping convention recorded in benchmarks/standard_bake_packing_2026-05-27.md + the QAT record ('identity ~97.7 exact, 0 above-identity') -- MEASURED to be a v47-era property: v47_strict_qat_native reads 97.6893, but shipped B reads 96.2412 and ADD156 reads 96.1157, so both shipped LINEAR dials fail it. Registered as specified 2026-09-04 and NOT relaxed; the incumbent's failure is a finding, not a reason to move the bar.

grids.label: dial_grid_372col_2026-05-29_quarantined (NOT canonical -- 9/115 w11 ladders + 33 pre-fix JXL d=0.025 cells; the grid benchmarks/imazen26_anchor_2026-09-04.md measured on)
grids.note: Registered ONLY so the 2026-09-04 imazen-26 anchor numbers (reach 96.85 / p5 13.73 / DR 85.99) stay checkable against their own instrument. New work should use the canonical grid; a verdict on this one carries bake_verdict's own NOT-CANONICAL warning.

negtail_probes.label: negtail_probe_372_2026-09-04 (kadis_negrich, 20 equal-count ssim2 quantile bins x 100, all rows ssim2 < 0)
negtail_probes.built_from: /mnt/v/zen/zensim-training/canonical-2026-07-15/train/kadis_negrich.parquet (266,111 rows; 237,675 with ssim2_gpu < 0). Selection is deterministic: 20 equal-count quantile bins over the negative population, lowest 100 row indices per bin. No RNG.
negtail_probes.truth_span: ssim2_gpu min -770.6197, p1 -187.1314, median -54.7239, max -0.3312 -- every row's reference metric is negative, so a correct dial must go below zero somewhere on it.
negtail_probes.incumbent_note: SHIPPED B never goes below zero on this probe (frac_below_zero 0.0000, min +2.5167) even though every row's truth is negative. That is a standing violation of the product contract ('NEGATIVE zensim values MUST work'), recorded here as the incumbent's own value so a candidate is judged on both the relative and the absolute question.

identity_probes.label: identity_probe_372_2026-09-04 (all 38 dial-grid reference images, ref == dist)
identity_probes.built_from: extract_features_372col --corpus pairs-tsv over the 38 distinct image_ids of the canonical dial grid, each paired with ITSELF, decoded by imazen codecs (zenpng) at this lane's HEAD.
identity_probes.measured_property: All 38 rows are the ZERO vector, bit-identical -- which is what a difference metric must do, and it makes the identity dial a SCALAR property of the bake, dial(0-vector). The probe is kept as 38 rows rather than 1 so that property stays gated rather than assumed.
identity_probes.incumbent_note: SHIPPED B calls a perfect copy 96.2412 while emitting up to 99.9833 on LOSSY dial-grid cells: 266 of 4,424 cells (6.01%) out-score an exact copy, worst `1a20ecb0c1b92466_1022x818` jxl d=0.05 at 99.9833. Standing ceiling defect, recorded as the incumbent's own value.
